@zachleat small addition to `npm install`'s cooldown feature:
there's also a `--min-release-age X` flag (https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-install#min-release-age) which acts similarly as the one in `pnpm` / `npm-check-updates`, delays packages to be at least X days old.

the `npm update` command also has this flag, and you can even put a `min-release-age` into your (or project's) `.npmrc`, or set via `export npm_config_min_release_age=X` in `.zshrc`!

(this info is courtesy of @stefan's web weekly newsletter from this week)

npm-install | npm Docs

@zachleat @stefan fun fact, the `min-release-age` is actually translated into a `before` variable every time `npm` resolves the config:

```
$ npm config set --location=user min-release-age=10
$ npm config list
; "user" config from /home/pcdevil/.npmrc

before = "2026-05-03T09:51:47.109Z"
```
